category: Layouts, Plotting, Sheet Sets & File Management
description: The output and file-handling commands that complement PLOT/PUBLISH/PAGESETUP/LAYOUT: the layout wizard, command-line page setup, viewport maximise, moving objects between spaces, exporting a layout to model space, the full -PLOT prompt sequence used by scripts, plot stamps, plot style tables and their editor, DWF/PDF export settings, exporting proxy-free drawings, sheet sets (manager, wizard, open), the viewport Express Tools, file open/save/close variants, DXF in/out, recovery, CAD standards, security and drawing history, and the session utilities (TIME, STATUS, SETVAR, text window, log file, VIEWRES, drawing properties, partial open, markup sets, backup folder, drawing logs).

tools.name: LAYOUTWIZARD
tools.description: Steps through creating a new layout: name, printer/plotter, paper size and units, orientation, an optional title block inserted as a block or xref from the Template folder, the viewport arrangement (none, single, standard 3D engineering views or an array) with its scale, and the viewport location. It writes a page setup into the layout, which is why it is a quick way to produce consistently configured sheets without a template.
tools.usage:
LAYOUTWIZARD
(Create Layout wizard pages: Begin [name] > Printer > Paper Size [units] > Orientation > Title Block [None / block list, Block or Xref] > Define Viewports [None / Single / Std. 3D Engineering Views / Array; viewport scale; rows/columns/spacing] > Pick Location [two corners] > Finish)

parameters.name: Printer
parameters.description: Any configured plotter or pc3 (e.g. DWG To PDF.pc3, None).

parameters.name: Title Block
parameters.description: DWG files found in the Template folder; inserted at 0,0 as block or xref.

parameters.name: Define Viewports
parameters.description: Std. 3D Engineering Views creates four viewports (top, front, side, isometric); Array creates rows x columns.

parameters.name: Viewport scale
parameters.description: Scaled to fit or a fixed scale from the scale list.

tools.example:
LAYOUTWIZARD
(Name: A1-SHEET-02; Printer: DWG To PDF.pc3; ISO A1, Millimeters; Landscape; Title block: none; Single viewport, scale 1:100; pick two corners; Finish)
tools.notes: Layouts created this way have their page setup stored unnamed; save it with PAGESETUP for reuse. LAYOUT N or the template route (LAYOUT T) is preferable when a company template exists.

tools.name: -PAGESETUP
tools.description: Command-line page setup (2021+): edits the current layout's plot device, paper size, plot area, scale, offset, plot style table, lineweight and shade options with the same prompt sequence as -PLOT, but stores the result in the layout (optionally as a named page setup) instead of plotting. It fills the gap that forced scripts to plot in order to change setups, and is the Core Console way to prepare layouts for PUBLISH.
tools.usage:
-PAGESETUP
(prompts mirror -PLOT's detailed configuration: layout name, output device, paper size, paper units, orientation, upside down, plot area, plot scale, plot offset, plot with plot styles, plot style table, plot with lineweights, scale lineweights, plot paper space first, hide paperspace objects, shade plot; then)
Save changes to page setup [Yes/No]? <N>: Y
Enter page setup name to save <>: <name>

parameters.name: layout name
parameters.description: Model or a layout name; ? lists layouts.

parameters.name: page setup name
parameters.description: A named page setup usable later in PLOT/PUBLISH and importable into other drawings with PAGESETUP > Import.

tools.example:
; script: set every layout to A3 PDF, 1:1, monochrome
-PAGESETUP
Layout1
DWG To PDF.pc3
ISO full bleed A3 (420.00 x 297.00 MM)
M
L
N
L
1:1
0,0
Y
monochrome.ctb
Y
N
N
N
Y
A3-PDF
tools.notes: Paper size names must match the pc3 exactly (use PLOT's dialog once to read them). The interactive PAGESETUP dialog remains the way to import named setups from a template.

tools.name: VPMAX
tools.description: Maximises a layout viewport to fill the drawing area so its model-space contents can be edited at full size without changing the viewport's scale or view; VPMIN restores the layout view, returning exactly to the previous zoom. A red border shows the maximised state, and the status-bar button or double-clicking the viewport border does the same. VPMAXIMIZEDSTATE reports the state.
tools.usage:
VPMAX  (with one viewport: maximises it; otherwise Select a viewport to maximize: <pick>)
VPMIN
VPMAXIMIZEDSTATE = 0 | 1 (read-only)
tools.example:
VPMAX
(pick the plan viewport)
(edit walls at 1:1 with the layout hidden)
VPMIN
tools.notes: Unlike MSPACE, editing while maximised cannot accidentally pan or zoom the viewport view (the view is restored by VPMIN). Locked viewports can be maximised too. Not available in the Core Console (no display).

tools.name: CHSPACE
tools.description: Moves objects between model space and paper space through a layout viewport, scaling them by the viewport's scale so they keep their visual size and position on the sheet: from paper space, selected objects (notes, dimensions, blocks) are pushed into the viewport's model space; from an active viewport, selected model-space objects are pulled onto the layout. Originally an Express Tool, core since 2007.
tools.usage:
CHSPACE  (run on a layout tab)
Select objects: <selection> Enter
(if several viewports are active/eligible) Select a viewport: <pick>
-> 'n object(s) changed from PAPER space to MODEL space' (or the reverse)

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Determined by which space is current: paper (PSPACE) sends to model; model inside a viewport (MSPACE) sends to paper.

parameters.name: scaling
parameters.description: Objects are scaled by the viewport scale factor and repositioned so they appear unchanged on the sheet; text heights change accordingly.

tools.example:
PSPACE
CHSPACE
(select the paper-space dimensions drawn over the plan) Enter
-> dimensions now live in model space at the correct scale
tools.notes: Annotative objects moved to model space get the viewport's annotation scale. Objects that cross viewport boundaries are still moved whole. Not available in the Model tab.

tools.name: EXPORTLAYOUT
tools.description: Exports the current layout to a new drawing whose model space contains everything visible on the layout - paper-space objects at 1:1 and the contents of each viewport projected, scaled and clipped as they appear on the sheet - producing a flat, single-space drawing for consultants who cannot handle layouts, or for DWG deliverables in plot coordinates. The Create Drawing dialog asks only for the file name.
tools.usage:
EXPORTLAYOUT
(Export Layout to Model Space Drawing dialog: file name .dwg)
-> 'The layout was successfully exported to <file>. Open the exported drawing?'

parameters.name: viewport contents
parameters.description: Objects are copied, scaled by the viewport scale and clipped to the viewport boundary; xrefs are bound; annotative objects use the viewport's scale representation.

parameters.name: paper units
parameters.description: The result uses the layout's paper units (mm or inches) as drawing units.

tools.example:
LAYOUT S A1-01
EXPORTLAYOUT
C:/issue/A1-01_flat.dwg
N
tools.notes: Objects hidden by layer visibility in the viewport are omitted; dimensions become non-associative copies. OLE objects and images are included; hatches are exploded where clipped. Works in the Core Console with FILEDIA 0.

tools.name: LAYOUTMERGE
tools.description: Express Tool that combines several layouts into one: the objects of each selected layout (including viewports) are moved into the destination layout side by side, optionally deleting the source layouts. It is used to consolidate old multi-layout drawings or to gather sheets for a single publish. -LAYOUTMERGE is the command-line form.
tools.usage:
LAYOUTMERGE
(Layouts to Merge dialog: tick layouts; Merge into: destination layout)
Delete empty layouts? [Yes/No] <Y>:
-LAYOUTMERGE
Enter layout name(s) to merge or [?] <*>:  Enter destination layout name:

parameters.name: destination layout
parameters.description: Existing layout that receives the objects; each merged layout's content is offset so they do not overlap.

parameters.name: Delete empty layouts
parameters.description: Remove the emptied source layouts afterwards.

tools.example:
-LAYOUTMERGE
Sheet2,Sheet3
Sheet1
Y
tools.notes: Page setups of merged layouts are lost (the destination keeps its own). Viewports from different layouts keep their scale. Not in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: -PLOT
tools.description: The command-line PLOT used by every plotting script, batch file and Core Console job: after 'Detailed plot configuration? Yes' it asks in a fixed order for layout, device, paper size, units, orientation, upside-down, plot area, scale, offset, plot styles, plot style table, lineweights, (layout only: scale lineweights, paper space first, hide paperspace objects; model only: shade plot), plot-to-file and file name, whether to save the page setup and finally whether to proceed. Answering No to the detailed question plots with the layout's current page setup after only the layout name and file prompts.
tools.usage:
-PLOT
Detailed plot configuration? [Yes/No] <No>: Y
Enter a layout name or [?] <Model>:
Enter an output device name or [?] <current>: DWG To PDF.pc3
Enter paper size or [?] <current>: ISO full bleed A1 (841.00 x 594.00 MM)
Enter paper units [Inches/Millimeters] <Millimeters>:
Enter drawing orientation [Portrait/Landscape] <Landscape>:
Plot upside down? [Yes/No] <No>:
Enter plot area [Display/Extents/Layout/View/Window] <Layout>:   (Model tab: Display/Extents/Limits/View/Window)
Enter plot scale (Plotted Millimeters=Drawing Units) or [Fit] <1:1>:
Enter plot offset (x,y) or [Center] <0.00,0.00>:
Plot with plot styles? [Yes/No] <Yes>:
Enter plot style table name or [?] (enter . for none) <>: monochrome.ctb
Plot with lineweights? [Yes/No] <Yes>:
Scale lineweights with plot scale? [Yes/No] <No>:      (layouts)
Plot paper space first? [Yes/No] <No>:                 (layouts)
Hide paperspace objects? [Yes/No] <No>:                (layouts)
Enter shade plot setting [As displayed/legacy Wireframe/legacy Hidden/Visual styles/Rendered] <As displayed>:   (Model)
Write the plot to a file [Yes/No] <N>: Y
Enter file name <drawing-layout.pdf>: C:/out/sheet.pdf
Save changes to page setup [Yes/No]? <N>:
Proceed with plot [Yes/No] <Y>:

parameters.name: Window
parameters.description: Plot area Window asks for two corners next (Enter lower left corner / upper right corner).

parameters.name: Fit
parameters.description: Scale to fit the paper; otherwise 1:1, 1:50, 1=2 or a factor.

parameters.name: plot style table
parameters.description: . (period) means none; ? lists the CTB/STB files on the plot style path.

parameters.name: BACKGROUNDPLOT
parameters.description: Set to 0 in scripts so the plot completes before the next command runs (1/3 plot in background).

parameters.name: PLOTOFFSET / PLOTROTMODE
parameters.description: Whether the offset is measured from the printable area edge (0) or the paper edge (1); how rotation is applied.

tools.example:
; PDF of a layout with the saved page setup, no questions asked
BACKGROUNDPLOT 0
-PLOT
N
A1-01
DWG To PDF.pc3
C:/out/A1-01.pdf
N
Y

; AutoLISP loop over all layouts
(foreach lay (layoutlist)
  (command "_.-PLOT" "_N" lay "DWG To PDF.pc3" (strcat "C:/out/" lay ".pdf") "_N" "_Y"))
tools.notes: The prompt sequence varies with the answers (No to detailed skips most; Model vs layout differs), so scripts must be written for one case. Paper size strings must match the pc3's names exactly. Output to system printers is not possible in the Core Console; pc3-based PDF/DWF works. PLQUIET 1 suppresses some dialogs, and FILEDIA/CMDDIA must be 0.

tools.name: PLOTSTAMP
tools.description: Configures the plot stamp - a line of text printed along the edge of every plot with fields such as drawing name, layout name, date and time, login name, device, paper size and plot scale, plus up to two user-defined fields - and optionally logs each plot to a file. Settings are saved in a .pss file (mm.pss / inches.pss by default) and the stamp is enabled per plot in the Plot dialog (Plot stamp on) or via -PLOTSTAMP for scripts.
tools.usage:
PLOTSTAMP
(Plot Stamp dialog: Plot stamp fields checkboxes; User defined fields; Plot stamp parameter file [Load/Save As]; Log file; Advanced: Location [Top left/Bottom left/Bottom right/Top right], Orientation, Stamp upside-down, X/Y offset relative to printable area or paper border, Font, Height, Single line plot stamp, Units, Log file location)
-PLOTSTAMP
Enter an option [On/OFF/Fields/User fields/Log file/LOCation/Text properties/UNits]:

parameters.name: Fields
parameters.description: Drawing name (with path), Layout name, Date and time, Login name, Device name, Paper size, Plot scale.

parameters.name: User fields
parameters.description: Two free strings, e.g. project number and revision, editable per plot.

parameters.name: Log file
parameters.description: Appends a line per plot (fields, date, user) to a text log - useful for print accounting.

parameters.name: PLOTSTAMP parameter file
parameters.description: .pss holding all settings; put a company file on the network and load it with -PLOTSTAMP.

tools.example:
-PLOTSTAMP
ON
-PLOTSTAMP
F
(answer Yes/No for each field: drawing name Y, layout Y, date Y, login Y, device N, paper N, scale Y)
-PLOTSTAMP
U
P-1042
REV C
tools.notes: The stamp is not part of the drawing; it is drawn by the plotter driver, so it appears in PDFs and DWFs but never on screen. Its position is measured inside the printable area, so on full-bleed paper sizes it can collide with title-block borders.

tools.name: PLOTSTYLE
tools.description: Assigns a named plot style to selected objects (or, with nothing selected, sets the current plot style for new objects) in drawings that use named plot style tables (STB, PSTYLEMODE 0); in colour-dependent drawings (CTB, PSTYLEMODE 1) the command is unavailable because colour decides the pen. CONVERTPSTYLES switches a drawing between the two modes and CONVERTCTB converts a .ctb file into a .stb file so the same pen assignments can be kept.
tools.usage:
PLOTSTYLE
Select objects: <selection> Enter   (or Enter with none selected to set the current plot style)
(Select Plot Style dialog: styles of the active plot style table, Active plot style table, Attached to layout)
CONVERTPSTYLES  (no prompts beyond confirmation; CTB drawing -> named styles, or named -> colour dependent)
CONVERTCTB  (Select File: .ctb -> Create File: .stb)

parameters.name: PSTYLEMODE
parameters.description: Read-only: 0 named plot styles (STB), 1 colour-dependent (CTB).

parameters.name: PSTYLEPOLICY
parameters.description: For new drawings: 0 named, 1 colour-dependent (also the Options > Plot and Publish > Plot Style Table Settings default).

parameters.name: CPLOTSTYLE
parameters.description: Current plot style name for new objects (BYLAYER, BYBLOCK, NORMAL or a style).

parameters.name: DEFPLSTYLE / DEFLPLSTYLE
parameters.description: Default plot style for new objects and for layer 0 in named-style drawings.

tools.example:
CONVERTCTB (monochrome.ctb -> office.stb)
CONVERTPSTYLES (in the drawing: Yes; choose office.stb)
PLOTSTYLE
(select the section lines) Enter
(choose Heavy)
tools.notes: Converting a drawing to named styles requires an STB whose style names you then assign per layer; xrefs must be in the same mode as the host or their styles are ignored. Most organisations stay with CTB for simplicity.

tools.name: Plot Style Table Editor
tools.description: The editor for .ctb and .stb files opened from STYLESMANAGER (double-click a table), from the Plot/Page Setup dialogs (Edit button) or by double-clicking the file in Explorer. It has General (description, apply global scale factor to non-ISO linetypes and fill patterns), Table View and Form View tabs; per colour (CTB, 255 entries) or per named style (STB) it sets the plotted Color, Dither, Grayscale, Pen number, Virtual pen, Screening (0-100%), Linetype, Adaptive adjustment, Lineweight, Line end style, Line join style and Fill style, with an Edit Lineweights list and Save As. The Add-A-Plot-Style-Table wizard in STYLESMANAGER creates new files.
tools.usage:
STYLESMANAGER > double-click monochrome.ctb (or any table)
Form View: select colours (Ctrl/Shift for several) > set Color = Black, Screening = 100, Lineweight = 0.25 mm ... > Save & Close
Table View: spreadsheet of all entries
Add-A-Plot-Style-Table wizard: Start from scratch / Use existing / Use My R14 Plotter Configuration (CFG) / Use a PCP or PC2 file; Color-Dependent or Named; file name

parameters.name: Color
parameters.description: Use object color, Black, or any colour; Black for monochrome plots.

parameters.name: Screening
parameters.description: Percentage of ink, 100 full; 30-50 gives grey backgrounds.

parameters.name: Lineweight
parameters.description: Use object lineweight or a fixed mm value - the classic colour-to-pen-width mapping.

parameters.name: Apply global scale factor to non-ISO linetypes
parameters.description: Scales linetypes/fill patterns in the table by a factor at plot time.

parameters.name: Plot style search path
parameters.description: OPTIONS > Files > Printer Support File Path > Plot Style Table Search Path (%APPDATA%\Autodesk\...\Plot Styles by default).

tools.example:
; Make a grey-background pen table
STYLESMANAGER
(double-click acad.ctb, Save As office.ctb; select colours 8 and 9, Screening 40, Color Black; colours 1-7 Color Black, Lineweight by colour: 1=0.18, 2=0.25, 3=0.35, 4=0.5, 5=0.7, 7=0.13; Save & Close)
tools.notes: CTB files are looked up by name at plot time, so every workstation and the Core Console/Design Automation bundle must carry the same file. True colours and colour-book colours are not mapped by CTB (they plot as-is unless the table's Color is Black), which is why pen-based standards use ACI colours 1-255.

tools.name: EXPORTSETTINGS
tools.description: Opens the Export to DWF/PDF Options dialog that governs EXPORTPDF, EXPORTDWF and EXPORTDWFX (the Output tab's Export drop-down): what to export (current layout, all layouts, or for model space display/extents/window), the page setup to use (current or an override set in the Page Setup Override dialog), password protection, whether block, layer and hyperlink information is included, bookmark creation, font handling (capture as geometry), and merge control (lines overwrite or merge). The values are stored in EXPORTPAGESETUP, EXPORTMODELSPACE, EXPORTPAPERSPACE and EXPORTEPLOTFORMAT.
tools.usage:
EXPORTSETTINGS
(Export to DWF/PDF Options dialog: Location / Filename prefix; Export [Current layout/All layouts] (paper space) or [Display/Extents/Window] (model space); Page setup [Current/Override] + Page Setup Override...; Password protection; Block information; Layer information; Merge control; PDF: Vector quality dpi, Raster image quality dpi, Font handling [Capture all/some/none], Include hyperlinks, Create bookmarks)
EXPORTDWFX  (Save As DWFx dialog; uses these settings)
EXPORTEPLOTFORMAT = 0 DWF | 1 DWFx | 2 PDF (format of the last export / default)

parameters.name: Page Setup Override
parameters.description: Plot device, paper size, plot style table, scale and orientation applied to every exported layout regardless of their own setups.

parameters.name: Layer information
parameters.description: Writes layers into the PDF/DWF so viewers can toggle them (and PDFLAYERS can use them when re-attached).

parameters.name: Merge control
parameters.description: Lines Overwrite or Lines Merge for overlapping objects.

parameters.name: PDFSHX
parameters.description: 1 embeds SHX text as searchable comments in the PDF.

tools.example:
EXPORTSETTINGS
(Export: All layouts; Page setup: Override -> DWG To PDF.pc3, monochrome.ctb; Layer information: Include; Create bookmarks: On; OK)
EXPORTPDF (file name; all layouts go into one multi-page PDF)
tools.notes: EXPORTPDF/EXPORTDWF differ from PLOT in that they can produce a multi-sheet file of all layouts in one go without a DSD; PUBLISH offers more control (sheet order, mixed drawings). The PDF driver options themselves (DWG To PDF.pc3 properties) still apply.

tools.name: EXPORTTOAUTOCAD
tools.description: Creates a copy of the drawing in which custom AEC/proxy objects from the AutoCAD Architecture, MEP, Civil 3D, Plant 3D and similar toolsets are exploded into plain AutoCAD objects (lines, polylines, blocks, text), optionally binding xrefs and saving to an older DWG format, so the file opens cleanly in plain AutoCAD or third-party software without object enablers. In plain AutoCAD it is the practical fix for drawings full of proxy objects; -EXPORTTOAUTOCAD gives the command-line prompts.
tools.usage:
-EXPORTTOAUTOCAD
Enter an option [Format/Bind/bind Type/Maintain/Prefix/Suffix/?] <eXport>: (set options) then Enter
Enter filename <drive:\path\ACAD-drawing.dwg>: <path>
Options: Format = 2018 / 2013 / 2010 / 2007 / 2004 / 2000 DWG; Bind xrefs Yes/No; bind Type Bind/Insert; Maintain resolved properties Yes/No; Prefix / Suffix for the new file name (default ACAD-)

parameters.name: Format
parameters.description: Target DWG version.

parameters.name: Bind / bind Type
parameters.description: Bind attached xrefs into the export (Bind or Insert naming).

parameters.name: Maintain resolved properties
parameters.description: Keep display properties (colours/linetypes from display representations) on the exploded objects.

parameters.name: Prefix / Suffix
parameters.description: Name of the exported file relative to the original.

tools.example:
-EXPORTTOAUTOCAD
F
2018
B
Y

C:/issue/ACAD-Plan.dwg
tools.notes: The exported file loses all AEC intelligence (walls become lines). PURGEAECDATA (2022+) removes invisible AEC dictionaries without exploding objects. The vertical products offer richer options in their own EXPORTTOAUTOCAD dialogs.

tools.name: -PUBLISH
tools.description: Publishes a drawing set described by a saved Drawing Set Description (.dsd) file without showing the Publish dialog: the DSD lists the drawings and layouts, their page setups, the output type (plotter, DWF, DWFx or PDF), file name and options such as multi-sheet vs single-sheet files. Combined with BACKGROUNDPLOT 0 it is how scripts and the Core Console batch-plot whole sets; acad.exe /pl file.dsd does the same from the Windows command line.
tools.usage:
-PUBLISH
Enter name of sheet list to load: <path.dsd>
(the set is published to the destination stored in the DSD; PUBLISHCOLLATE decides single multi-sheet file vs one file per sheet)
Create the DSD interactively once: PUBLISH > add sheets > Save Sheet List (.dsd)

parameters.name: .dsd contents
parameters.description: INI-style text: [DWF6Version], [DWF6MinorVersion], [Target] (Type=6 PDF single-sheet, 5 PDF multi-sheet, DWF/DWFx types, plotter), OUT= output path, [Sheet]/[sheet list] entries with DWG=, Layout=, Setup=, OriginalSheetPath=, Has Plot Port=...

parameters.name: PUBLISHCOLLATE
parameters.description: 1 one multi-sheet file, 0 one file per sheet.

parameters.name: PUBLISHALLSHEETS
parameters.description: 1 (default) includes all layouts of the current drawing when PUBLISH starts, 0 only the current.

parameters.name: BACKGROUNDPLOT
parameters.description: 0 foreground (required for scripts), 1 background plot, 2 background publish, 3 both.

parameters.name: BGCOREPUBLISH
parameters.description: 2022+: whether background publishing uses multiple cores.

tools.example:
BACKGROUNDPLOT 0
-PUBLISH
C:/proj/1042/issue03.dsd

; Windows batch
"C:\Program Files\Autodesk\AutoCAD 2025\acad.exe" /pl "C:\proj\1042\issue03.dsd"
tools.notes: DSD paths are absolute; edit the file with a text editor (or generate it) to point at other drawings. Publishing to a system printer needs the full AutoCAD; PDF/DWF output works in the Core Console. Sheet set publishing writes the same DSD behind the scenes.

tools.name: SHEETSET
tools.description: Opens the Sheet Set Manager (alias SSM, Ctrl+4): a palette that organises the layouts of many drawings into a named, ordered set stored in a .dst file, with subsets, sheet numbers and titles, sheet-set and custom properties usable as fields in title blocks, resource drawings whose named views become sheet views, callout and label blocks, page setup overrides from a template, and one-click Publish/eTransmit/Archive of the whole set or a selection. Since 2026.1.1 the same palette handles cloud (Autodesk Docs) sheet sets as the Connected Sheet Set Manager with multi-user editing. SHEETSETHIDE closes it.
tools.usage:
SHEETSET  (alias SSM; View tab > Palettes)
(tabs: Sheet List [subsets, sheets, Publish, eTransmit, Archive, Properties, Insert Sheet List Table], Sheet Views [categories, views from resource drawings, place callout blocks], Model Views [resource drawing folders])
SHEETSETHIDE
System variables: SSMSTATE (open?), SSMAUTOOPEN (open the set's SSM when a sheet drawing opens), SSMPOLLTIME / SSMSHEETSTATUS (refresh interval and lock status), SSLOCATE (locate sheet set on opening a drawing), SSMDETECTMODE, SSMOPENMODE (2026.1.1: how cloud DSTs open)

parameters.name: Sheet set properties
parameters.description: Name, description, sheet storage location, sheet creation template (layout in a .dwt), page setup overrides file, project number/name/phase/milestone and custom properties (sheet-set or per-sheet).

parameters.name: Fields
parameters.description: %<\AcSm SheetSet.ProjectNumber>%, SheetNumber, SheetTitle, CurrentSheetSubSet... inserted in title-block attributes so every sheet updates from the set.

parameters.name: Publish
parameters.description: Publish to Plotter / DWF / DWFx / PDF, using each sheet's page setup or a page setup override; Sheet Selections save subsets to publish.

parameters.name: Insert Sheet List Table
parameters.description: A table of sheet numbers and titles on the cover sheet that updates when the set changes.

tools.example:
OPENSHEETSET C:/proj/1042/1042.dst
SHEETSET
(right-click the set > Publish > Publish to PDF; choose the override page setup; the whole set becomes one PDF)
tools.notes: Sheet sets require each layout to belong to exactly one set; a layout used in two sets gives 'already in a sheet set'. Keep the .dst with the drawings on a network path everyone maps identically. The Sheet Set Manager for Web (2023-2026) was removed in 2026.1.1 in favour of the Connected SSM.

tools.name: NEWSHEETSET
tools.description: Runs the Create Sheet Set wizard: start from an example sheet set (a .dst template such as Architectural Metric Sheet Set with its subsets and title-block layouts) or from existing drawings (importing their layouts as sheets, optionally creating subsets from the folder structure and prefixing sheet titles with the file name), name the set, choose where the .dst is stored and set its properties, then confirm. It is the starting point for any project that will use fields, callouts and set-wide publishing.
tools.usage:
NEWSHEETSET  (Sheet Set Manager > drop-down > New Sheet Set; File > New Sheet Set)
(Create Sheet Set wizard: Begin [An example sheet set / Existing drawings] > Sheet Set Example (list of example .dst) or Sheet Set Details [name, description, Store sheet set data file here, Sheet Set Properties...] > Choose Layouts [Browse folders, Import Options: Prefix sheet titles with file name, Create subsets based on folder structure, Ignore top level folder] > Confirm > Finish)

parameters.name: An example sheet set
parameters.description: Copies the example's structure, template and properties without sheets.

parameters.name: Existing drawings
parameters.description: Scans folders and imports every layout (initialised layouts only, those that have been activated at least once).

parameters.name: Sheet Set Properties
parameters.description: Sheet creation template, page setup overrides file, resource drawing locations, callout/label blocks, custom properties.

tools.example:
NEWSHEETSET
(Existing drawings; name 1042-SET; store C:\proj\1042; Sheet Set Properties: template C:\std\A1.dwt layout A1-SHEET; Browse C:\proj\1042\sheets, tick Create subsets from folders; Finish)
tools.notes: Layouts that have never been opened are not initialised and are skipped by the import - open them once. A drawing's layouts can only be in one set.

tools.name: OPENSHEETSET
tools.description: Opens a sheet set data file (.dst) in the Sheet Set Manager by path from the command line, without the file dialog when FILEDIA is 0 - which is how scripts and CUI macros load a project's set before publishing or before opening sheets. The recently used sets are also listed in the SSM drop-down and on the Start tab.
tools.usage:
OPENSHEETSET
Enter sheet set file name: <path.dst>   (or Open Sheet Set dialog when FILEDIA is 1)

parameters.name: .dst path
parameters.description: Local or UNC path; cloud sets (Autodesk Docs) open through the Connected SSM per SSMOPENMODE.

parameters.name: ENABLEDSTLOCK
parameters.description: 2022+: whether a DST opened from Autodesk Docs/BIM 360 is locked for others.

tools.example:
FILEDIA 0
OPENSHEETSET
C:/proj/1042/1042.dst
; then publish it
(the SSM's Publish to PDF, or -PUBLISH with the DSD the SSM saved)
tools.notes: A .dst is a small database; opening it from two machines simultaneously is supported with a lock (.dst.lock? no - SSM uses an internal lock recorded in the file) and stale locks are reported by SSMSHEETSTATUS. Copying a .dst without its drawings breaks the sheet references.

tools.name: VPSYNC
tools.description: Express Tool that aligns the views of several layout viewports with a master viewport: the selected viewports are panned so the model-space geometry lines up with the master's, which is what plan and section viewports or a plan split across two viewports need. The viewports keep their own scales; use VPSCALE first to check them and ALIGNSPACE for arbitrary point alignment.
tools.usage:
VPSYNC
Select master viewport: <pick>
Select viewports to be aligned with the master viewport: <pick> Enter
VPSCALE
Select edge of viewport: <pick>  -> 'PS:MS == 1:50' (paper-to-model ratio of the viewport)
tools.example:
VPSCALE (pick the plan viewport) -> PS:MS == 1:100
VPSYNC
(pick the plan viewport)
(pick the two adjacent plan viewports) Enter
tools.notes: Only the view centre is changed, not the scale or the viewport frame. Lock the viewports afterwards (Properties > Display locked = Yes) so zooming inside them does not undo the alignment. Not in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: ALIGNSPACE
tools.description: Express Tool that pans and, with two points, zooms a layout viewport so that picked model-space points coincide with picked paper-space points - for example to make a gridline in the viewport land exactly on a paper-space title-block reference mark. One point pair pans only; two pairs also set the scale to fit.
tools.usage:
ALIGNSPACE
Select model space alignment point(s): <one or two points inside the active viewport> Enter
Select paper space alignment point(s): <matching one or two points in paper space> Enter

parameters.name: one point
parameters.description: The viewport is panned so the model point sits on the paper point.

parameters.name: two points
parameters.description: Pan plus zoom (scale) so both pairs coincide; the resulting scale is usually not a standard one - use VPSCALE to check.

tools.example:
MSPACE (activate the viewport)
ALIGNSPACE
(pick gridline intersection A1) Enter
(pick the crosshair mark on the sheet) Enter
tools.notes: Run it from paper space with the target viewport identified by the first pick, or activate the viewport first. Not in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: PSBSCALE
tools.description: Express Tool that sets or updates the scale of block references in model space relative to paper space, so symbols (north arrows, section markers, tags) appear at a constant paper size in viewports of different scales - the pre-annotative solution to the scaling problem. PSTSCALE does the same for text objects. Both remember the desired paper size and can be re-run (Update) after viewport scales change.
tools.usage:
PSBSCALE
Select objects: <block references> Enter
Enter an option [Set/Update] <Set>:
Set: Specify paper space block scale <1.0>: <factor>  (block scale relative to paper)
PSTSCALE
Select objects: <text> Enter
Enter an option [Set/Update] <Set>:
Set: Specify paper space text height <2.5>:

parameters.name: Set
parameters.description: Store the paper-space scale/height in the object's xdata and apply it for the current viewport scale.

parameters.name: Update
parameters.description: Recalculate the model-space scale from the stored value after the viewport scale changed.

tools.example:
MSPACE (in the 1:200 viewport)
PSBSCALE
(select the north arrow) Enter
S
1
tools.notes: Annotative blocks and text (2008+) replace this workflow; PSBSCALE remains for drawings that must stay non-annotative. Not in LT.

tools.name: NEW
tools.description: Starts a new drawing from a template (.dwt) chosen in the Select Template dialog (or, when STARTUP is 1, through the Create New Drawing dialog with Start from Scratch, Use a Template and Use a Wizard); QNEW skips the dialog and uses the default template set in Options > Files > Template Settings > Default Template File Name for QNEW (or, if none, asks). The Start tab's New button runs QNEW. Command-line scripts use NEW with FILEDIA 0 and a template path, or acad.exe /t.
tools.usage:
NEW  (Ctrl+N)
(Select Template dialog: .dwt; the Open button's arrow offers Open with no Template - Imperial / Metric)
with FILEDIA 0: Enter template file name or [. (for none)] <acadiso.dwt>: <path.dwt> | .
QNEW  (uses the QNEW default template; asks for one if none is set)
STARTUP = 0 Start tab off / 1 Create New Drawing dialog and Startup dialog / 2 Start tab (default) / 3 Start tab, new drawing opened at start

parameters.name: template
parameters.description: acad.dwt / acadiso.dwt (imperial/metric), acad3D.dwt, Tutorial templates, or company templates from the Template File Location path.

parameters.name: . (period)
parameters.description: No template: a blank drawing with default settings (MEASUREINIT decides imperial/metric).

parameters.name: SDI
parameters.description: 1 forces single-document mode (only one drawing open) - used by some legacy apps.

tools.example:
FILEDIA 0
NEW
C:/std/A1-Metric.dwt

; AutoLISP (opens in a new document; the rest of the routine does not run there)
(vla-Add (vla-get-Documents (vlax-get-acad-object)) "C:/std/A1-Metric.dwt")
tools.notes: In the Core Console NEW is not allowed; the console opens its own drawing (from /i or a default). Drawings created with . (no template) are unitless; set INSUNITS and the scale list yourself.

tools.name: CLOSE
tools.description: Closes the current drawing, prompting to save if it was modified (the prompt can be answered in scripts); CLOSEALL closes every open drawing with the same prompt per drawing, CLOSEALLOTHER (2016+) closes all but the current one, and QUIT/EXIT closes the application. In scripts the sequence QSAVE then CLOSE avoids the prompt, and (command "_.CLOSE" "_Y") answers it in LISP - although LISP itself stops running once its document closes.
tools.usage:
CLOSE            Save changes to <drawing>? [Yes/No/Cancel] (only if modified)
CLOSEALL         (prompts per modified drawing)
CLOSEALLOTHER    (closes all except the current)
QUIT / EXIT      (closes AutoCAD after the save prompts)

parameters.name: DBMOD
parameters.description: Read-only bit code showing what was modified (1 objects, 4 database variables, 8 window, 16 view, 32 field); non-zero means CLOSE will prompt.

parameters.name: Yes / No
parameters.description: No discards changes; drawings that were never saved ask for a file name on Yes.

tools.example:
; script line pair for batch processing in the full AutoCAD
QSAVE
CLOSE

; discard changes without prompting
CLOSE
N
tools.notes: In the Core Console the drawing is closed automatically when the script ends; CLOSE there ends the session. A drawing opened read-only closes without a prompt. CLOSE on the last drawing leaves AutoCAD open with no document (zero-doc state).

tools.name: SAVE
tools.description: Always opens the Save Drawing As dialog (or, with FILEDIA 0, prompts for a name) and saves a copy under that name without changing which file is current - unlike QSAVE, which saves in place, and SAVEAS, which switches the session to the new name. The Express Tool SAVEALL saves every open drawing. Behind all of them, ISAVEPERCENT controls incremental saves, ISAVEBAK the .bak creation and SAVEFORMAT/DWGCHECK-related settings the version and checks.
tools.usage:
SAVE
(Save Drawing As dialog; with FILEDIA 0: Save drawing as <current name>: <path>)
SAVEALL  (Express Tool: saves all open drawings, prompting for names of unnamed ones)
Related variables: ISAVEPERCENT (0 full save every time, default 50), ISAVEBAK (0 no .bak), SAVEFIDELITY (annotative visual fidelity), SAVEFILEPATH / SAVEFILE (autosave folder and current .sv$ name), SAVETIME (autosave minutes)

parameters.name: copy semantics
parameters.description: The current drawing keeps its original name and modified state; the copy is written in the current DWG format unless the dialog's Files of type is changed.

parameters.name: ISAVEPERCENT
parameters.description: Allows wasted space in the DWG to speed saves; 0 forces a full save which keeps files smaller.

parameters.name: ISAVEBAK
parameters.description: 1 (default) writes drawing.bak on every save; 0 disables it (faster on slow networks).

tools.example:
FILEDIA 0
SAVE
C:/backup/plan_before_cleanup.dwg
-PURGE A * N
QSAVE
tools.notes: SAVE to the same name as the current drawing behaves like QSAVE. In the Core Console SAVE/QSAVE/SAVEAS are the way to write results; a drawing loaded with /i is not saved unless the script does it.

tools.name: DXFOUT
tools.description: Writes the drawing (or selected objects) as a DXF file in a chosen DXF version (AutoCAD 2018 down to R12/LT2), ASCII or binary, with a chosen number of decimal places, through the Save Drawing As dialog's DXF file types and its Options; with FILEDIA 0 the command-line prompts allow scripted exports. DXF is the documented exchange format read by CAM, GIS, laser cutters and libraries like ezdxf.
tools.usage:
DXFOUT
(Save Drawing As dialog: Files of type AutoCAD 2018 DXF / 2013 / 2010 / 2007 / 2004 / 2000 / R12/LT2 DXF; Tools > Options: Select objects, Format ASCII/Binary, Decimal places of accuracy 0-16)
FILEDIA 0:
Enter file name: <path.dxf>
Enter decimal places of accuracy (0 to 16)/Objects/Binary <16>: <n> | O | B

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Older versions drop objects the version cannot represent (MLEADER, tables, dynamic blocks become proxies or are exploded); R12 DXF is the most widely read by non-CAD tools (no LWPOLYLINE, polylines become POLYLINE/VERTEX).

parameters.name: Objects
parameters.description: Export a selection only (the file still has HEADER/TABLES but only those entities).

parameters.name: Binary
parameters.description: Smaller and faster to parse, but fewer readers support it.

parameters.name: decimal places
parameters.description: Precision of coordinates written; 16 is the default (full double).

tools.example:
FILEDIA 0
DXFOUT
C:/out/plate.dxf
16

; R12 for a laser cutter via SAVEAS
SAVEAS
R12
C:/out/plate_r12.dxf
tools.notes: SAVEAS with a DXF type makes the DXF the current file; DXFOUT does not. DXF files do not carry raster images or xref content - only the references. The DXF Reference documents every group code (Developer Documentation on help.autodesk.com).

tools.name: DXFIN
tools.description: Reads a DXF file: into a brand-new, empty drawing it imports everything (header variables, tables, blocks, entities, objects) so the result is a faithful drawing; into a drawing that already has content it imports only the entities and block definitions, ignoring header and table settings that conflict. OPEN can also read DXF directly, which is the normal route; DXFIN is for scripts and for merging DXF geometry into an existing drawing.
tools.usage:
DXFIN
(Select File dialog: .dxf)
FILEDIA 0: Enter file name: <path.dxf>

parameters.name: empty drawing
parameters.description: Start with NEW using no template (.) for a complete import including limits, units and layers.

parameters.name: non-empty drawing
parameters.description: Entities are added; existing layers/styles of the same name win; 'DXF file is not fully compatible' messages are normal.

tools.example:
FILEDIA 0
NEW
.
DXFIN
C:/in/survey.dxf
SAVEAS
2018
C:/in/survey.dwg
tools.notes: Malformed DXF (wrong handles, missing ENDSEC) aborts with 'Invalid or incomplete DXF input' and a line number; fix the file or use ODA File Converter to normalise it. Coordinates are taken as-is; check INSUNITS after import.

tools.name: RECOVERALL
tools.description: Repairs a damaged drawing together with all of its attached xrefs (nested ones included), running the same checks as RECOVER on each file and reporting the results in a Drawing Recovery Log; the repaired xrefs are saved in place (backups are made) so the host opens cleanly. Use it when RECOVER fixes the host but the xrefs still report errors.
tools.usage:
RECOVERALL
(Select File dialog: the host .dwg; FILEDIA 0: Enter name of drawing file to recover:)
(Drawing Recovery Log dialog: per-file errors found/fixed; Continue)

parameters.name: backups
parameters.description: Each repaired xref is first copied to <name>.bak (or _recover) before being overwritten.

parameters.name: RECOVERAUTO
parameters.description: 0 prompt before recovering a damaged drawing on open, 1 recover silently, 2 recover silently with a log.

tools.example:
RECOVERALL
C:/proj/1042/host.dwg
(review the log; Continue)
AUDIT Y
QSAVE
tools.notes: Cannot run while the host is open - it opens the file itself. Xrefs that are read-only or locked by other users are skipped. Follow with -PURGE and AUDIT in the host.

tools.name: DRAWINGRECOVERY
tools.description: Opens the Drawing Recovery Manager, the palette that appears after a crash listing every drawing that was open with its recoverable files - the autosave .sv$, the backup .bak, the last saved .dwg and the recovered copy - with details (date, size) and a preview, so the newest good version can be opened and saved under the original name. DRAWINGRECOVERYHIDE closes it; RECOVERYMODE controls whether recovery info is recorded and shown.
tools.usage:
DRAWINGRECOVERY
(Drawing Recovery Manager palette: Backup Files tree per drawing [Drawing name, Drawing.sv$, Drawing.bak, Drawing_recover.dwg], Details, Preview; double-click to open a file)
DRAWINGRECOVERYHIDE
RECOVERYMODE = 0 no recovery information recorded | 1 recorded, manager shown after a crash (default) | 2 recorded, manager shown and the recovered drawing opened automatically

parameters.name: .sv$
parameters.description: Autosave file written every SAVETIME minutes to SAVEFILEPATH (default %TEMP%); rename to .dwg to open manually if the manager is not available.

parameters.name: .bak
parameters.description: Previous version copied at each save when ISAVEBAK is 1; MOVEBAK can redirect it.

parameters.name: .dwl / .dwl2
parameters.description: Lock files next to an open drawing; a stale one after a crash makes the file open read-only - delete it when no session has the drawing open.

tools.example:
DRAWINGRECOVERY
(expand PLAN.dwg, double-click PLAN_1_1_1234.sv$ - the newest; check it; SAVEAS PLAN.dwg)
tools.notes: Autosave files are deleted when the drawing is closed normally, so they exist only after a crash. Set SAVETIME to 5-10 minutes on unstable systems; 0 disables autosave.

tools.name: CHECKSTANDARDS
tools.description: Checks the current drawing against the CAD standards files (.dws) associated with it by STANDARDS, comparing layers, dimension styles, linetypes and text styles (the standard plug-ins) and stepping through each violation with a proposed replacement and Fix / Next / Mark as ignored buttons; Fix renames or re-properties the non-standard item to the standard one. The status-bar standards icon and STANDARDSVIOLATION provide real-time notification; the separate Batch Standards Checker (DwgCheckStandards.exe) audits many drawings to an HTML report.
tools.usage:
STANDARDS  (Configure Standards dialog: Standards tab - add .dws files with + and order them; Plug-ins tab - tick Dimension Styles, Layers, Linetypes, Text Styles; Settings...)
CHECKSTANDARDS
(Check Standards dialog: Problem, Replace with [standard items], Preview of changes, Fix, Next, Mark this problem as ignored, Settings, Close -> summary)
STANDARDSVIOLATION = 0 off | 1 display alert on violation | 2 status bar icon (default)

parameters.name: .dws file
parameters.description: A drawing saved as AutoCAD Drawing Standards containing the approved layers, styles and linetypes; several can be associated, the first has priority.

parameters.name: Settings
parameters.description: Notification options; Automatically fix non-standard properties; Show ignored problems; Preferred standards file to use for replacements.

parameters.name: Batch Standards Checker
parameters.description: Standalone tool (Start menu / DwgCheckStandards.exe) that checks a list of drawings against .dws files and writes .chx report files viewable as HTML.

tools.example:
STANDARDS
(add C:\std\office.dws; Plug-ins: all; OK)
CHECKSTANDARDS
(Problem: Layer 'WALLS' - Name is non-standard; Replace with A-WALL; Fix; Next ... Close)
tools.notes: Standards check names and properties; they do not enforce block libraries or content. Fixing a layer name merges objects onto the standard layer. Associated standards are stored in the drawing (ACAD_DWS dictionary) and travel with it.

tools.name: STANDARDS
tools.description: Opens the Configure Standards dialog to associate one or more CAD standards files (.dws) with the current drawing and to choose which plug-ins (Dimension Styles, Layers, Linetypes, Text Styles) are checked, in what priority order; it is the setup step for CHECKSTANDARDS and for the real-time notification icon. A .dws is created simply by SAVEAS with the AutoCAD Drawing Standards file type from a drawing that contains the approved named objects.
tools.usage:
STANDARDS
(Configure Standards dialog: Standards tab [Standards files associated with the current drawing: + add, x remove, up/down order; Description] ; Plug-ins tab [checkboxes per plug-in, purpose/version]; Settings; Check Standards... button)
Create a standards file: SAVEAS > Files of type: AutoCAD Drawing Standards (*.dws)

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: When several .dws define the same name, the first in the list wins for replacements.

parameters.name: plug-ins
parameters.description: Third-party plug-ins can add checks (e.g. block or attribute standards) through the CAD Standards API.

tools.example:
; create the standard once
OPEN C:/std/office_template.dwg
SAVEAS
DWS
C:/std/office.dws
; associate in project drawings
STANDARDS (add office.dws, OK)
tools.notes: The association is saved in each drawing; put it in the template so every new drawing is covered. LAYTRANS uses .dws/.dwg/.dwt files as layer-name mapping sources independently of STANDARDS.

tools.name: SECURITYOPTIONS
tools.description: Opens the Security Options dialog for the drawing's digital signature: attach a digital signature (from a certificate in the Windows store) after saving, with a time stamp from a time server and a comment, so recipients can verify the file has not changed since signing. DIGITALSIGN (2016+) is the direct command for signing, SIGVALIDATE checks signatures of the current drawing and its xrefs, and SIGWARN controls the warning dialog on opening signed files. The old password-protection tab was removed in 2016; encryption must be done outside AutoCAD.
tools.usage:
SECURITYOPTIONS
(Security Options dialog: Digital Signature tab - Attach digital signature after saving drawing, Select a digital ID (certificate), Signature information: Get time stamp from [time server], Comment)
DIGITALSIGN  (same digital-signature dialog)
SIGVALIDATE  (Validate Digital Signatures dialog: status, view base signature, xref signatures)
SIGWARN = 0 warn only if the signature is invalid | 1 always show the signature dialog when opening a signed drawing

parameters.name: digital ID
parameters.description: A certificate with a private key installed in the Windows certificate store (from a CA or self-signed via the Windows tools).

parameters.name: time stamp
parameters.description: Optional trusted time from an internet time server.

parameters.name: signature validity
parameters.description: Any change to the DWG after signing (including a save) invalidates the signature.

tools.example:
QSAVE
DIGITALSIGN
(tick Attach digital signature after saving; choose the company certificate; comment 'Issued for construction'; OK)
QSAVE
tools.notes: Signatures are stored in the DWG and survive copying but not saving from another application (e.g. DWG TrueView convert). The Windows Explorer shell extension shows a signature icon on signed DWGs. Drawing passwords from 2015 and earlier still open with the password prompt but cannot be set.

tools.name: DWGHISTORY
tools.description: Opens the Drawing History palette (2021+) showing the version history of the current drawing when it is stored in a cloud service that keeps versions - Autodesk Docs/Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Box, Google Drive - with the date, user and version of each save; a version can be compared with the current drawing (running DWG Compare) or opened. DWGHISTORYCLOSE closes it and DWGHISTORYSTATE reports its state.
tools.usage:
DWGHISTORY  (View tab > History > Drawing History)
(palette: version list with filters by date range / user / minimum time between versions; Compare button per version)
DWGHISTORYCLOSE

parameters.name: supported storage
parameters.description: The drawing must be opened from a folder synchronised by the desktop client of the cloud service (or Desktop Connector for Autodesk Docs); local/network files show no history.

parameters.name: Compare
parameters.description: Downloads the selected version to a temporary file and runs COMPARE against the current drawing.

tools.example:
(open C:\Users\me\Dropbox\proj\PLAN.dwg)
DWGHISTORY
(filter last 30 days; select the version from Monday; Compare)
tools.notes: Version retention is the cloud service's policy, not AutoCAD's. Activity Insights (2024+) records the same kind of events for any location and adds 'What's changed' comparisons in 2026.

tools.name: TIME
tools.description: Displays the drawing's time statistics on the text screen - current time, creation time, last update time, total editing time, an elapsed timer that can be started, stopped and reset, and the time of the next automatic save - and lets you control the elapsed timer. The values are also available as system variables (TDCREATE, TDUPDATE, TDINDWG, TDUSRTIMER) and fields, which is how title blocks show 'total hours'.
tools.usage:
TIME
Current time / Times for this drawing: Created, Last updated, Total editing time, Elapsed timer (on), Next automatic save in
Enter option [Display/ON/OFF/Reset]: <keyword> | Enter to exit

parameters.name: Display
parameters.description: Repeat the listing with updated times.

parameters.name: ON / OFF / Reset
parameters.description: Control the user elapsed timer (TDUSRTIMER).

parameters.name: TDCREATE / TDUPDATE
parameters.description: Julian date reals of creation and last save; TDUCREATE/TDUUPDATE are the UTC versions.

parameters.name: TDINDWG
parameters.description: Total editing time in days (fraction) - multiply by 24 for hours.

tools.example:
TIME
D

; AutoLISP: hours spent in the drawing
(* 24 (getvar "TDINDWG"))

; field for a title block
%<\AcVar TdinDwg \f "%tc4%lu6%pt4">%
tools.notes: Total editing time accumulates while the drawing is open, whether or not anyone is working, and can be reset only by copying objects into a new drawing (or third-party tools). The Express Tool EDITTIME tracks active time instead.

tools.name: STATUS
tools.description: Prints a summary of the drawing state on the text screen: number of objects, model or paper space limits and extents (with 'Over' flags when objects exceed the limits), display extents, insertion base point, snap and grid spacing, current space, layout, layer, colour, linetype, material, lineweight, elevation and thickness, the mode toggles (Fill, Grid, Ortho, Qtext, Snap, Tablet), the active object snap modes, and free space on the drawing and temp drives plus free physical memory and swap. It is the first diagnostic when a drawing behaves oddly (huge extents, wrong space).
tools.usage: STATUS  (no prompts; output on the text window, F2)

parameters.name: Extents
parameters.description: Compare with the geometry you expect; extents far from the model indicate stray objects (find them with ZOOM E then QSELECT).

parameters.name: Free dwg disk / temp disk
parameters.description: Low temp space causes save failures and crashes.

tools.example:
STATUS
-> 1,842 objects in C:\proj\PLAN.dwg
   Model space limits are X: 0.0000 Y: 0.0000 ... (Off)
   Model space uses  X: -12.5 Y: -3.2  **Over  ...
tools.notes: In LISP the same information is available via getvar (EXTMIN/EXTMAX, LIMMIN/LIMMAX, CLAYER...). STATUS inside DIMSTYLE or the old DIM prompt shows dimension variables instead.

tools.name: SETVAR
tools.description: Reads or sets any system variable by name, including read-only ones (displayed only), and lists variables with wildcards. Most variables can be typed directly at the command prompt, but SETVAR is needed when a variable name collides with a command name (e.g. AREA, GRID? no - AREA is both) and it is the transparent way ('SETVAR) to change a setting in the middle of another command. It is also the safe form in scripts because the prompt sequence is always name then value.
tools.usage:
SETVAR
Enter variable name or [?] <last>: <name> | ?
? -> Enter variable(s) to list <*>: <wildcard>  (lists names and values, page by page)
Enter new value for <name> <current>: <value>
'SETVAR (transparent, inside another command)

parameters.name: read-only variables
parameters.description: Shown with '(read only)'; setting them errors.

parameters.name: wildcards
parameters.description: DIM* lists all dimension variables, *SCALE all scale-related ones.

tools.example:
SETVAR
AREA
(shows the last computed area, which typing AREA would not, since AREA runs the command)

; inside LINE, switch orthomode on transparently
LINE
'SETVAR
ORTHOMODE
1
(continue picking points)
tools.notes: Variables changed in a script that is not run with /isolate persist in the user's registry when they are user settings; drawing variables persist in the DWG when saved. SYSVARMONITOR can flag changes to critical ones.

tools.name: TEXTSCR
tools.description: Opens the AutoCAD Text Window, a separate window showing the full command history (all prompts, LIST output, STATUS, script echo) with copy and paste; GRAPHSCR returns focus to the drawing. F2 toggles the extended command history in the docked command line instead (or the Text Window when the command line is floating/hidden). LIST, STATUS, TIME and DBLIST write there, and CLIPROMPTLINES / CLIPROMPTUPDATE control how much appears in the temporary prompt area.
tools.usage:
TEXTSCR  (or F2)
GRAPHSCR  (or F2 again)
CLIPROMPTLINES = number of temporary prompt lines shown above the command line (0-50)
CLIPROMPTUPDATE = 0 suppress messages during scripts/LISP | 1 show them

parameters.name: copy history
parameters.description: Right-click > Copy History puts the whole session log on the clipboard - handy for support requests together with ACADINFO.

parameters.name: LOGFILEON
parameters.description: Writes the same text to a log file continuously.

tools.example:
LIST (select the polyline)
TEXTSCR
(read the vertex list; right-click > Copy History)
GRAPHSCR
tools.notes: In scripts TEXTSCR is used before long listings so they are visible; in the Core Console everything is already text. The window keeps up to the CMDINPUTHISTORYMAX / history buffer size of lines.

tools.name: LOGFILEON
tools.description: Starts writing the text of the command window (prompts, responses, listings) to a log file until LOGFILEOFF or the drawing closes; the file is named after the drawing plus a session suffix in LOGFILEPATH, and LOGFILEMODE / LOGFILENAME reflect the state and current name. It is the simplest audit trail for batch scripts, for capturing BCOUNT or LIST output, and for reproducing problems.
tools.usage:
LOGFILEON
LOGFILEOFF
LOGFILEMODE = 0 off | 1 on (read-only reflection of the state; also settable)
LOGFILEPATH = folder (OPTIONS > Files > Log File Location)
LOGFILENAME = current log file (read-only), e.g. C:\Users\me\AppData\Local\Autodesk\...\PLAN_1_1_1234.log

parameters.name: file naming
parameters.description: <drawing>_<n>_<n>_<n>.log per session; old logs are not deleted automatically.

parameters.name: OPTIONS > Open and Save > Maintain a log file
parameters.description: Turns logging on for every session.

tools.example:
; script that records what happened
LOGFILEON
-PURGE A * N
AUDIT Y
BCOUNT

LOGFILEOFF
tools.notes: In the Core Console, redirect stdout instead (accoreconsole ... > log.txt) - LOGFILEON also works there. Logging does not capture dialog interactions.

tools.name: VIEWRES
tools.description: Sets the display resolution of circles, arcs and ellipses (circle zoom percent, 1-20000, default 1000) that decides how many segments curves are drawn with on screen; too low and circles look like polygons after zooming, too high and regeneration slows on large drawings. The 'fast zooms' question is historical and ignored. WHIPARC 1 displays true circles instead of vectors, REGENAUTO controls whether regenerations happen automatically, and REDRAW/REDRAWALL merely refresh the screen without regenerating.
tools.usage:
VIEWRES
Do you want fast zooms? [Yes/No] <Y>:
Enter circle zoom percent (1-20000) <1000>: <n>
WHIPARC = 0 (vectors, default) | 1 (smooth circles/arcs)
REGENAUTO  Enter mode [ON/OFF] <ON>:   (REGENMODE)
REDRAW / REDRAWALL  (refresh the current / all viewports; also clears blips and marker glyphs)

parameters.name: circle zoom percent
parameters.description: Higher = smoother; affects display only, never plots (plots use the plotter resolution).

parameters.name: REGENAUTO OFF
parameters.description: Suppresses automatic REGENs after changes that need them; AutoCAD asks 'About to regen, proceed?' - only for huge legacy drawings.

tools.example:
VIEWRES
Y
5000
REGEN
tools.notes: VIEWRES is saved in the drawing. Hardware acceleration makes the setting less relevant, but drawings that look faceted after opening from other systems usually just need VIEWRES raised and REGEN.

tools.name: DWGPROPS
tools.description: Opens the Drawing Properties dialog (General, Summary, Statistics, Custom tabs): Summary holds title, subject, author, keywords, comments and the hyperlink base; Statistics shows created/modified dates, last saved by and total editing time; Custom holds user name/value pairs. All of them are available as fields (Title, Author, Custom properties) for title blocks and are searchable in DesignCenter and Windows Explorer, which makes DWGPROPS the drawing-level metadata store when no sheet set is used.
tools.usage:
DWGPROPS  (File > Drawing Properties)
(dialog: General [file info]; Summary [Title, Subject, Author, Keywords, Comments, Hyperlink base]; Statistics; Custom [Add / Delete name-value pairs])
Field usage: %<\AcVar Title>%  %<\AcVar Author>%  %<\AcVar CustomDP.ProjectNo>%

parameters.name: Hyperlink base
parameters.description: Same as HYPERLINKBASE; root for relative hyperlinks.

parameters.name: Custom properties
parameters.description: Name/value strings; the Express Tool PROPULATE can fill them in batch, and the ActiveX SummaryInfo object reads/writes them.

tools.example:
DWGPROPS
(Summary: Title 'Ground floor plan', Author 'BS'; Custom: ProjectNo = 1042, Rev = C; OK)
FIELD (Document category > Title) placed in the title block
tools.notes: Properties are stored in the DWG's summary info stream and survive SAVEAS but not WBLOCK. In .NET they are Database.SummaryInfo; in COM AcadDocument.SummaryInfo.

tools.name: PARTIALOPEN
tools.description: Opens only part of a large drawing - the geometry of selected layers and/or a named view - so that huge site or plant drawings load quickly; the rest can be brought in later with PARTIALOAD. Reached from the Open dialog's Open drop-down (Partial Open) or by -PARTIALOPEN at the command line, which asks for the file, the view and the layers. Spatial and layer indexes (INDEXCTL) saved in the drawing make partial loading much faster.
tools.usage:
-PARTIALOPEN
Enter name of drawing to open: <path.dwg>
Enter view to load or [?] <*Extents*>: <view name>
Enter layers to load or [?] <none>: <layer names, comma separated, or wildcards>
Unload all Xrefs on open? [Yes/No] <N>:
PARTIALOAD  (Partial Load dialog: pick a view and layers to add to the partially open drawing)
PARTIALOPEN dialog: OPEN > Open drop-down > Partial Open

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: Only objects inside the view's window are loaded (with a spatial index); *Extents* loads all geometry on the chosen layers.

parameters.name: layers
parameters.description: Objects on other layers are not loaded at all; the layers exist but are empty until PARTIALOAD.

parameters.name: INDEXCTL
parameters.description: 0 none, 1 layer index, 2 spatial index, 3 both (set in the drawing before saving).

tools.example:
-PARTIALOPEN
C:/proj/site_master.dwg
BLOCK-7
C-TOPO*,C-ROAD*
N
tools.notes: A partially open drawing is fully functional but saving it keeps the unloaded objects untouched; xrefs are loaded per the Unload answer. PARTIALOAD cannot remove already-loaded layers. Not available in the Core Console or for DXF files.

tools.name: MARKUP
tools.description: Opens the Markup Set Manager, which loads DWF/DWFx markup sets created in Autodesk Design Review (red-lines, comments, stamps on published sheets) and displays each markup over the corresponding layout so it can be reviewed, its status set (New, Question, For Review, Done), and the sheets republished with the markups; OPENDWFMARKUP opens a marked-up DWF directly, MARKUPCLOSE closes the palette and MSMSTATE reports it. It is the legacy review round-trip that Markup Import/Assist (PDF and image markups, 2023+) now complements.
tools.usage:
MARKUP  (alias MSM; Ctrl+7)
(Markup Set Manager palette: Open a markup set .dwf/.dwfx; tree of sheets and markups; Details/Preview; View Redline Geometry / View DWG Geometry / View DWF Geometry toggles; Republish Markup DWF)
OPENDWFMARKUP  (Select File: .dwf/.dwfx containing markups)
MARKUPCLOSE

parameters.name: markup status
parameters.description: Per markup: <None>, Question, For Review, Done - written back into the DWF when republished.

parameters.name: Republish
parameters.description: Republish All Sheets / Republish Markup Sheets after edits so the reviewer's DWF shows the changes.

tools.example:
OPENDWFMARKUP
C:/review/issue03_marked.dwfx
(double-click a markup to open its sheet; fix the drawing; set status Done; Republish Markup Sheets)
tools.notes: Design Review is no longer developed but still available; Autodesk Docs / the AutoCAD web app markups use Trace and Markup Import instead. The markups themselves are never written into the DWG.

tools.name: MOVEBAK
tools.description: Express Tool that redirects the .bak backup files created at each save to a chosen folder instead of the drawing's own folder, keeping project directories clean; setting the value to a period restores the default. The path is stored in the registry per user.
tools.usage:
MOVEBAK
Enter new value for MOVEBAK, or . for none <current>: <folder path> | .

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description: Existing folder; backups are named <drawing>.bak inside it, so drawings with the same name from different projects overwrite each other.

tools.example:
MOVEBAK
C:/CAD/bak
tools.notes: Loaded with Express Tools (EXPRESSTOOLS if the menu is missing); the setting is applied by an acad.lsp-level reactor so it persists across sessions. ISAVEBAK 0 disables backups entirely.

tools.name: DWGLOG
tools.description: Express Tool that creates and maintains a per-drawing log file (<drawing>.log next to the DWG) recording when the drawing was opened, saved and closed and by whom, giving a simple access history for shared project files without a document management system. It is switched on or off for the session, and the log accumulates over time.
tools.usage:
DWGLOG
Enter an option [ON/OFF] <current>:  (writes 'Opened by <user> on <date time>' style entries)
tools.example:
DWGLOG
ON
(open and save drawings; each gets a .log beside it)
tools.notes: Requires write access to the drawing folder. Activity Insights (2024+) supersedes it with a central, searchable event log. Not in LT.

tools.name: ACADINFO
tools.description: Express Tool that writes a text report about the AutoCAD installation and session - product version and build, profile, support paths, loaded ObjectARX/.NET applications, key system variables, operating system and hardware - to a file (acadinfo.txt by default) for support tickets and CAD-management audits.
tools.usage:
ACADINFO
Enter a filename to save the information to <acadinfo.txt>: <path>
tools.example:
ACADINFO
C:/support/acadinfo_ws12.txt
tools.notes: The report contains user paths and may include license details; review before sharing. The core alternative is About > Product Information plus (arx) / (vl-list-loaded-vlx) listings and the SYSVDLG export.
